title: feat(fleet-write): advisory_versions drops a listed package by name and admits a pre-release range bound
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"huangyiirene"} -->
_Requested by **Irene** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01TJXtQ1tVD26ecLDZxFS67x?thread=cmsg_01TJXtQ1tVD26ecLDZxFS67x8Be2AAcUBhodBsvnWLd3Xs)_

Fixes #37005

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 用户无感（内部工具）：安全席位在发布安全公告前，现在可以按名字明确删掉一个被误列的受影响软件包，也可以把预发布版本写进受影响版本范围的上下界。
- 为安全发布这条线解决：六条已获批准的安全公告因为无法删掉误列的软件包而停在草稿状态，本次之后可以继续发布。
- 出错时最坏的情况是那一次修改被拒绝或回读失败，公告留在草稿、不会被发出去；本次改动可以直接撤回。
- 无。

## What changes

The relay row `advisory_versions` (`scripts/pm/fleet-write`) gains the two capabilities the card asks for. The PATCH body is unchanged: it is still `{ vulnerabilities }`, built from the action's entries alone.

**1. An explicit `drop`.** The row now takes an optional `drop`: a quiet list of npm package names, capped like a draft's `packages`.
- **Fence (executor, nothing sent, exit 5).** A listed package counts as named when `versions` sets it or `drop` removes it. The existing count, "N listed package(s) the action does not name", still refuses any listed package that neither one names, so a silent drop is still impossible. A `drop` name the advisory does not list is refused at the same `versions` fence.
- **Validator (before any request, exit 2).** It refuses a `drop` entry that is not an npm name, a duplicate, an empty list, more than ten names, a non-array, and a name that `versions` also sets. The last check is a new row key, `disjointPackages: ['drop', 'versions']`, judged by `advisoryDropOverlap`.
- **Read-back.** The stored list must equal the sent entries (unchanged), and no dropped name may remain. When one does, the action is FAILED with `drop[i] still listed — a package the action dropped`.
- **Landed row.** It adds `· dropped N package(s)`, a count only.
- **Echo discipline.** Every refusal and printed line names a drop entry by its position (`drop[1]`), never by its name. See the acceptance notes.

**2. Pre-release range bounds.** `ADVISORY_VERSION_RANGE_SHAPE` now admits a pre-release of a release version in every comparator, for example `>= 17.0.0-rc.6, < 18.6.0`, `< 19.0.0-next.1` or `= 16.0.0-rc-1`.
- The tag is semver 2.0.0's: one to four dot-separated identifiers, with no leading zero in a numeric identifier, each identifier capped. A build tag is still refused.
- `compareReleaseVersions` is replaced by `compareAdvisoryVersions`, which compares by semver precedence. A pre-release sorts below its release, and identifiers compare numerically, then as words. Both the rising-bounds check and the patched-not-inside-range check use it.
- `patched_versions` stays release-only. Its refusal now says so by name: "a pre-release is a range bound only, never a patched version".

**Docs.** The relay header row for `advisory_versions` in `ops.mjs` is updated, along with its prose (the versions row section, the echo rules and the executor's path), the op-table key list, and the matching header lines in `validate.mjs` and `execute.mjs`. As the card says, the lane charter is not edited.

**Landing.** As expected: `ops.mjs`, `validate.mjs` and `execute.mjs`. `dispatch.mjs` needs no change, because the seat side never reads the row's keys.

## Why

On 2026-11-24, six maintainer-approved advisory publications stopped at the `versions` fence. Five only drop a package; one adds a package and drops another. In each case the corrected list leaves out a package the report listed but the fix never touched. Today the relay has no way to drop such a package, so the only routes are to publish a false "affected" or to wait for the maintainer to delete the package by hand in the GitHub UI. Separately, fixes first released in an `-rc.N` or `-next.N` prerelease had their lower bounds raised to the first stable release, which leaves prerelease installs unreported.

## Tests

Self-tests, all run on HEAD `fc06281d`:

- `node scripts/pm/fleet-write/validate.mjs --self-test` ⇒ `✓ fleet-write/validate self-test: 463 cases pass across 23 batteries` (453 on main). The advisory battery floor rises from 80 to 90.
- `node scripts/pm/fleet-write/execute.mjs --self-test` ⇒ `✓ fleet-write/execute self-test: 464 cases pass across 31 batteries` (460 on main). The advisory battery floor rises from 42 to 46, and the marker sweep pin from 75 runs to 82.
- `node scripts/pm/fleet-write/dispatch.mjs --self-test` ⇒ `✓ fleet-write/dispatch self-test: 430 cases pass across 34 batteries` (unchanged).

New pins, in the existing `advisory_versions` batteries:

- **Op table (closed shape).** `advisory_versions` takes the optional key `drop`. `FIELDS.drop` is a quiet npm-name list. No other row takes `drop` or declares `disjointPackages`. A drop never reaches the body; it rides the descriptor as a copy.
- **Validator, one refusal per bad input:**
  - a non-npm entry;
  - a name that `versions` also sets (named by position, singular and plural);
  - an empty `drop`;
  - a name twice;
  - eleven names;
  - a string;
  - an object entry;
  - prose in `drop` (never echoed);
  - `versions: []` beside a `drop`, and `drop` without `versions`.
- **Ranges.** Accepted: seven pre-release spellings, including GitHub's own example `>= 3.4.0-rc.0, <= 3.4.9`. Refused: fourteen malformed or build-tagged spellings, and four pre-release pairs whose bounds do not rise. A patched version inside a range with a pre-release lower bound is refused; one at the range's exclusive upper bound passes. A pre-release patched version is refused and the refusal says why. The semver ladder from the specification is pinned.
- **Fence.** Landed cases: a drop alone, a drop beside an added package, two drops, and a drop of a package listed by name only. Refused cases: a drop naming an unlisted package, and an unnamed listed package beside a drop of another. Each is pinned in `validate.mjs` (pure), and in `execute.mjs` as "not sent, exit 5" with no package name in what was printed.
- **Read-back.** Landed with a drop, and the landed row text. FAILED when the answer still lists a dropped package: one write, never re-sent.
- **Executor gate.** The validator gate inside the executor makes zero requests for a drop that overlaps `versions` and for a drop carrying prose.

<details><summary>Ablations (one per changed behaviour; mutated with scripts/ablation-replace.mjs, restored to the HEAD blob each time)</summary>

| mutation | validate | execute | red cases |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| fence ignores `drop` (named = versions only) | 1 (2 failed) | 1 (3 failed) | fence accepted/refused with a drop; executor dropped, drop-fenced, drop-kept |
| validator overlap check off | 1 (2 failed) | 1 (1 failed) | drop refused, overlap; executor gate before any request |
| pre-release no longer below its release | 1 (3 failed) | 0 | accepted spellings, patched inside a pre-release range, semver ladder |
| read-back drops its `still listed` clause | 1 (1 failed) | 1 (1 failed) | read-back with a drop (both files) |

Each restore printed `ok restored: blob == HEAD … and git diff HEAD is empty`. The executor staying green on the third mutation is expected: the end-to-end pre-release case lands under either comparison.
</details>

## Acceptance notes

- **The empty-list refusal is structurally impossible (Zone 2, H3: confirmed).** `versions` is required with at least one entry (`validateField` kind `versions`: "must name at least one entry"). The PATCH replaces the list with exactly those entries, so a drop can never leave the advisory with no entry. This is pinned as the validator refusal of `versions: []` beside a `drop`, plus `versions` staying required beside a `drop`. The header states it in prose.
- **Echo discipline (H4: the stricter reading taken).** The card allows a refusal to echo the package name; the existing header (`advisoryVersionEntryFailure`) forbids echoing any value before the publish. Every drop refusal, fence sentence and read-back line names the entry by its position (`drop[1]`), never by its name. Pinned in the validator overlap case, the fence sentence and the executor's printed rows.
- **Where each refusal lives (H2: confirmed).** "Not listed" is judged only against the executor's own GET, so it is an executor fence (exit 5, not sent). "In both", "non-npm", the cap, duplicates and the closed shape are validator refusals made before any request.
- **Pre-release measurement (H5).** The platform accepts a pre-release in `vulnerable_version_range`, so the validator now admits one.
  - GitHub's guide "Best practices for writing repository security advisories" (`github/docs`, `content/code-security/tutorials/fix-reported-vulnerabilities/write-security-advisories.md`, read from `main` on 2026-11-24, sha256 `9188f67a33fa…`) says: "The version must begin with a number followed by any number of numbers, letters, dots, dashes, or underscores (anything other than a space or comma)."
  - Its examples include `>= 3.4.0-rc.0, <= 3.4.9`, `>= 15.0-rc-1, < 15.5.5` and `= 16.0.0-rc-1`, and it states that `2.0.0-alpha`, `2.0.0-beta` and `2.0.0-rc` are earlier than `2.0.0`.
  - GitHub's REST OpenAPI description (`github/rest-api-description`, `api.github.com.json`) types `repository-advisory-update.vulnerabilities[].vulnerable_version_range` as `{"type":"string","nullable":true}` with no pattern. Its examples are release-only, so it does not settle the question by itself.
  - A live relay run is impossible before merge, because the relay executes main's scripts. The first live run after merge confirms this reading.
- **`patched_versions` stays release-only (Zone 3).** The guide also shows pre-release patched versions (`32.0.0-android`). The card names the range bounds only, so admitting pre-release patched versions is left for a card that asks for it.
- **Seat-side hint.** A drop-only correction sends `versions` with the entries that stay, in the row's spelling, plus `drop` for the packages to remove. One that adds and drops sends both.
- **Contract review.** This diff touches no contract face of `references/contract-review.md` and no governed surface (only `scripts/pm/fleet-write/**`).

## Verification

**Read first (by risk):**
1. `scripts/pm/fleet-write/ops.mjs`: the `versions` fence in `ADVISORY_FENCES`. The silent-drop guard is now "listed minus versions minus drop", plus the unlisted-drop clause.
2. `scripts/pm/fleet-write/ops.mjs`: `BOUND_VERSION` / `ADVISORY_VERSION_RANGE_SHAPE` and `compareAdvisoryVersions`, which control which ranges are admitted and the patched-inside check.
3. `scripts/pm/fleet-write/validate.mjs`: the `disjointPackages` block in `validateAction`.

**Two-minute check:** run `node scripts/pm/fleet-write/validate.mjs --self-test && node scripts/pm/fleet-write/execute.mjs --self-test`. Expect `463 cases pass across 23 batteries`, then `464 cases pass across 31 batteries`.

<details><summary>Local gates on fc06281d</summary>

- Derived gates: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 63 families for the 3 changed paths (279 changed lines).
- `--ran` reconciliation: `✓ dispatch-gates --ran: 63 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 62 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED (1 DERIVED from a recorded exit 3)`.
- Each of the 62 run families exited 0. They include `check:pm-fleet-write-validate`, `check:pm-fleet-write-execute`, `check:pm-fleet-write-dispatch`, `check:pm-dispatch-gates`, `check:pm-governed-merges`, `check:nul-bytes`, `check:commit-card-trailers` and `check:issue-citations`.
- NOT MEASURED: `check:i18n-coverage`, because its prerequisite, a built workspace CLI (`packages/cli/dist`), was missing. This diff builds no package, so the result is left to CI.
- `node scripts/pm/overlap-check.mjs`: `VERDICT clean exit 0` (0 PR heads share these files).
- `node scripts/check-commit-card-trailers.mjs --range origin/main..HEAD`: clean.
</details>

## Human Minimum

- [x] 1. Schemas start as Zod; `packages/spec` holds no runtime logic. (No `packages/spec` change.)
- [x] 2. Every name I added uses the casing for its kind.
- [ ] 3. No formatter ran; `pnpm lint` passes. (No formatter ran; lint is CI's `Lint & Repo Gates`.)
- [x] 4. One issue, one branch off an up-to-date `main`, one pull request.
- [x] 5. A change that publishes carries a changeset, and both declaration lines are filled in here and in the changeset. (`scripts/pm/**` publishes nothing: `skip-changeset`.)
- [x] 6. `packages/spec` touched: its generated artifacts are regenerated and committed. (Not touched.)
- [x] 7. No hand edits to `content/docs/references/`, `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` or `content/docs/releases/`.
- [x] 8. Title, body and comments are in English.
- [x] The *Before Submitting* list in CONTRIBUTING.md is done.
